status_summary: H.R. 1226, the Restoring Checks and Balances Act, was introduced in the House on 2025-02-12 and referred to Oversight and Government Reform and Judiciary; it would make rules issued by any agency after enactment, including HHS, expire five years after taking effect unless reauthorized by an Act of Congress, with agencies reporting a justification before reauthorization. It is a government-wide statutory sunset for new rules rather than a codification of the HHS SUNSET rule's review-or-expire design for existing regulations, so it is recorded as a parallel match. No HHS rule reinstating the SUNSET rule was found; a Federal Register search shows no SUNSET document since HHS withdrew the January 2021 rule on 2022-05-27. Executive Order 14270, signed 2025-04-09, and H.R. 7592, introduced 2026-02-17, apply conditional sunsets only to energy-related agencies and do not cover HHS.

timeline.event: H.R. 1226, the Restoring Checks and Balances Act, was introduced in the House; it would sunset new rules of all agencies, including HHS, five years after they take effect unless reauthorized by Congress.

title: Reinstate the HHS SUNSET rule and have Congress codify regulatory expiry
uncertainties: Checked systematically on 2026-10-18. The Federal Register API check (the full SUNSET rule name, and a variant on retrospective review and expiry limited to HHS) found no SUNSET document since the 2022 withdrawal; the 20 of 35 HHS results read were payment, program and deregulatory rules with no expiry mechanism. The Unified Agenda check was partial: only the Federal Register fallback was usable. The Congress check read on govinfo the status records and introduced texts of H.R. 7592, which covers only DOE, FERC and four Interior offices, and H.R. 1226, which sunsets new rules of all agencies after five years unless Congress reauthorizes them; the status records of H.R. 274 (sunset of rules upheld under Chevron deference) and S. 485 (congressional approval of major rules, with annual designation of existing major rules) were read but not their texts. Treating H.R. 1226 as a parallel step is a judgment call, since it differs from the HHS rule in covering only new rules and relying on congressional reauthorization; not_started is also defensible. The agency check read the HHS regulations, deregulatory agenda and retrospective review pages, which describe a request for information and reviews under existing executive orders, with no automatic expiry. The news check returned only 2020 to 2021 coverage. Executive Order 14270 was read by an earlier researcher for its covered-agency list. In a further review on 2026-10-18 the H.R. 1226 status record was re-read on govinfo.gov (two original cosponsors, all actions dated 2025-02-12, nothing later), and a Federal Register API check on the SUNSET rule's full title since 2025-01-20 again returned no documents.
